To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

serotonin 5‐HT _{2} receptor agonists potentiate the activity of N‐m‐D‐asparagine (NMDA‐)receptors via phospholipase C‐mediated hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol‐4,5‐bisphosphate and subsequent activation of protein kinase C.

serotonin 5‐HT(2) receptors modulate NMDA receptor activity by activating phosphoinositol‐hydrolysis and protein kinase C. This modulation of the NMDAR is a mechanism for the control of NMDA receptor activation and thus of the excitatory neurotransmission.
serotonin 5‐HT _{2} receptor activation enhances N‐methyl-D-aspartate receptor‐induced currents by a protein‐kinase C‐dependent mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of NMDA receptor activity.
the role of the 5-HT2A receptors in the regulation of NMDA receptor activity and the subsequent modulation of the NMDAR‐mediated currents.
the effects of serotonin (5‐HT) on N‐methyl-D-aspartate (N‐MDA) receptor function in Xenopus oocyte‐injected with RNA of rat brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the serotonin 5‐HT1A receptor subtype is involved in the regulation of the 5‐HT‐mediated enhancement of NMDAR‐mediated currents in rat hippocampal neurons, and that the enhancement of N‐metyld‐aspartate‐receptor (NMDA‐R)‐mediated currents by serotonin is mediated by a protein kinase‐C‐dependent mechanism.
the activation of 5‐HT 2 receptors leads to an increase of the NMDAR‐mediated ion current by a protein kinase‐C‐dependent mechanism.
serotonin enhances NMDA receptor mediated currents by a PKC‐dependent mechanism via 5‐HT 2 receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5‐Ht2A receptor stimulation can potentiate NMDA receptor mediated currents by a mechanism involving PKC.

5-HT2 receptors enhance N‐methyl-D‐aspartate‐receptor function via phosphoinositid hydrolysis and stimulation of PKC, and that this effect is mediated by a 5‐hydroxy‐tryptamine 2 (5‐HT2) receptor subtype.
5‐ht2 receptors potentiate nmda‐mediated ion channels through the activation of a phosphoinositide‐mediated pathway, which in turn activates protein kinase C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
serotonin 5‐HT receptors potentiate the NMDA‐mediated responses by activating a PKC‐dependent signaling pathway.
serotonin 5‐HT 2 receptors can modulate the activity of NMDA receptors via a PKC‐dependent mechanism.
serotonin can potentiate the NMDA receptors.
